reconcile.note: Gill identifies Luke's level place as a lower, level spot on the very mountain Matthew names, so the two Gospels describe one location rather than two conflicting settings.

discrepancy.emptyNote: D. F. Strauss judged the mountain-versus-plain settings a genuine inconsistency and considered the harmonizing single-location and single-episode readings unconvincing.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: D. F. Strauss (1808-1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846).

sides.snippet: Seeing the multitudes, he went up onto the mountain. When he had sat down, his disciples came to him.
sides.verseText: Seeing the multitudes, he went up onto the mountain. When he had sat down, his disciples came to him.

sides.snippet: He came down with them, and stood on a level place, with a crowd of his disciples… who came to hear him and to be healed of their diseases;
sides.verseText: He came down with them, and stood on a level place, with a crowd of his disciples, and a great number of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem, and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, who came to hear him and to be healed of their diseases;
